# agent-policy

> One command policy for coding agents (Claude Code and Codex): allow, ask and hand-off tiers written once in TOML, rendered to each agent's native permission rules, enforced further by a shared PreToolUse guard hook, plus a scratchpad helper for throwaway containers.
> Apache License 2.0. Author: Ivan Pinatti (https://github.com/ivan-pinatti).
> Canonical repository: https://github.com/ivan-pinatti-labs/agent-policy

## What it does

Decides, for every shell command a coding agent wants to run, whether it runs without asking, asks, or is handed to the user. The same policy is installed for Claude Code (a managed settings drop-in, covering every profile) and Codex (prefix rules and an administrator hook). A guard hook, run by both agents, checks what a command prefix cannot express: flags anywhere on the line, container mounts, and containers that belong to a protected deployment.

## Key files

- [README.md](README.md): what it is, requirements, usage
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the two layers, how each agent receives them, how the guard reads a command
- [docs/POLICY.md](docs/POLICY.md): tiers, rule format, how to change a rule
- [docs/SCRATCHPAD.md](docs/SCRATCHPAD.md): the agent-scratch helper
- [docs/OPERATIONS.md](docs/OPERATIONS.md): install, update both ways, harvest, protected deployments
- [policy/](policy/): the rules, one TOML file per area
- [hooks/guard](hooks/guard): the PreToolUse hook
- [lib/agent_policy/](lib/agent_policy/): command parsing and checks
- [tools/render.py](tools/render.py): renders the policy for each agent

## Tech stack

- Python 3.11+ standard library (guard, agent-scratch, renderer, tests with unittest)
- Bash (tools/collect.sh)
- Podman (test container, agent-scratch)
- Claude Code managed settings, Codex execpolicy rules and hooks

## Conventions

- Conventional Commits for commit messages, no ticket prefix baked in
- pre-commit hooks wired up via
  [ivan-pinatti-labs/pre-commit-checklists](https://github.com/ivan-pinatti-labs/pre-commit-checklists),
  see [.pre-commit-config.yaml](.pre-commit-config.yaml)
- Every policy or guard change comes with a test case; nothing machine specific is committed
